justification: Scratch registry v3 records whether a scratch owns a managed instance root or a historical source-root identity. Version 3 migrates v1 and v2 rows to layout legacy while preserving their recorded root, so destroy still withdraws the old route owner.

Doctor findings gain a CertificateTrustDetails member ({ trustStores }) so the certs check carries typed per-store trust rows. Existing members are unchanged; consumers that switch on the known shapes keep working and can ignore the new one.

RuntimeProvider.destroy is replaced by bringDown; its receipt is BringDownOutcome, whose removed arm carries the same volume counts, skipped volumes, and shutdown observations plus per-container receipts. No persisted state or command result embeds DestroyOutcome.

RuntimeProvider.removeObservedService is replaced by bringDownObserved; its receipt is ObservedBringDown, which reports the per-container action with the same optional shutdown observations. No persisted state or command result embeds ObservedServiceRemoval.
The command variant of RunProps accepts an optional capture. Existing command, shell, and library props are unchanged.
HelpCommandTargetDescriptor gains advertisedFormats field on all variants. The anyOf schema widened by one optional field; existing consumers that do not read advertisedFormats are unaffected.

Doctor gains a lando-roots section that reports root-owned files under Lando's own roots. Existing section ids are unchanged; consumers that filter on known sections keep working and can ignore the new id.

The meta:setup result becomes a union discriminated by dryRun: `lando setup --dry-run` returns the planned host changes (each with its exact commands and, when a step reads input, the manual commands a person can run instead), what this run would do with each (`approval`: approved, will-ask, will-skip, blocked, or not-offered) and the flags that approve it without a terminal (`approvedBy`), and how a run would get administrator access (`elevation`), while a finished setup adds dryRun: false and one hostChanges outcome per planned change, with the digest of any input a step piped to root. Consumers that read a finished setup keep every field they read before.

Version 3 records physical upgrade snapshots and their version-series evidence without inventing a live server version. The migrator decodes version 1 and 2 sidecars unchanged, preserving their existing server-version and SQLite metadata.

The new physical upgrade reason carries data-series evidence, which is separate from an observed server version. Existing server and SQLite snapshots keep their recorded version and all ownership and generation fields.

ProviderSetupPlan and its closed provider-only change union are replaced by the open HostChange contract (with HostChangePlanEntry and HostChangeOutcome), which covers provider, CA, router, and core host changes with exact commands, consent class, requirement, and undo. The removed schema was never persisted and never shipped in a release.

AppPlan and AppliedAppPlan services, including the same plans embedded in events and other surfaces, gain only the additive optional ServicePlan.dataVersion field. Applied-state v14 reads v13 records unchanged with the contract absent.

Plan-embedding events and the renderer's view of those events gain only additive optional ServicePlan.dataVersion fields inside the embedded plan. No event tag, required field, or previous event shape changes.

Every existing ServicePlan arm gains only additive optional dataVersion. The arms keep their previous required fields and constraints; applied-state v14 decodes v13 records unchanged with the contract absent.

Unreleased. Router routes are reported in a required `routes` list beside `connections`; `connections` holds listeners and publications only. A wildcard route is a `hostMatch: pattern` entry with no `url`. Scratch route entries use the same address fields (`host`, `protocol`, `pathPrefix`, `hostMatch`) in place of `hostname` and `scheme`. No persisted store embeds these shapes.
